questions.q: What is dbatools' native cmdlet for automated index and statistics maintenance?
options: Invoke-DbaDbOptimize
Optimize-DbaIndex
Update-DbaStatistics
Repair-DbaFragmentation
questions.explain: Invoke-DbaDbOptimize is dbatools' own command for the fragmentation-driven skip/reorganize/rebuild decision, plus statistics updates.

questions.q: What does -UpdateStatistics do when passed to Invoke-DbaDbOptimize?
options: Folds statistics maintenance into the same pass as index maintenance, instead of requiring a separate step
Deletes all statistics on the database
Only updates statistics, skipping index maintenance entirely
Has no real effect and is included for backward compatibility
questions.explain: It combines both maintenance concerns — index fragmentation and stale statistics — into one automated pass.

questions.q: How does the lesson suggest a shop already using Ola Hallengren's IndexOptimize procedure automate maintenance in PowerShell, without abandoning that procedure?
options: Call it via Invoke-DbaQuery (or Invoke-Command), letting PowerShell handle scheduling, logging, and error handling around the existing T-SQL logic
There is no way to use Hallengren's procedure from PowerShell
Rewrite IndexOptimize entirely as a native PowerShell function
Manually run it by hand every day instead of automating it
questions.explain: Invoke-DbaQuery lets PowerShell orchestrate around a trusted existing T-SQL procedure rather than forcing a full replacement.

questions.q: Why does index maintenance specifically benefit from the -WhatIf and try/catch patterns from earlier lessons?
options: It's a destructive-adjacent operation — a rebuild failing partway through, or running against the wrong database by typo, is a real production risk
Index maintenance cannot throw errors under any circumstances
-WhatIf is required syntax for Invoke-DbaDbOptimize to run at all
It has nothing to do with safety, only performance
questions.explain: The chapter's premise is that automation needs the same safety discipline as any other risky, unattended maintenance operation.

questions.q: In Invoke-DbaDbOptimize's fragmentation handling, what does the lesson say happens at low fragmentation?
options: It's skipped — no rebuild or reorganize needed
It always triggers a full rebuild regardless of level
It deletes the index entirely
It always triggers a reorganize regardless of level
questions.explain: Low fragmentation (roughly under 10%) doesn't need remediation at all — the same threshold logic from the manual T-SQL approach in the DBA course.
